chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Uqda narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Abdullah al-Muhammadi narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Sharif ibn Sabiq al-Taflisi, from al-Fadl ibn Abu Qurra al-Taflisi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, that he said:

The believers are tested, then Allah distinguishes them. Indeed, Allah did not exempt the believers from the calamities and hardships of this world, but He secured them within it from blindness and wretchedness in the Hereafter.
Then he said: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali used to lay his martyrs side by side, then say: 'Our martyrs are the martyrs of the prophets.'
ai.seo_question: How are believers distinguished from others through trials according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that divine testing is a mechanism for distinguishing true believers rather than a sign of divine abandonment, ensuring their ultimate salvation from the 'blindness' of the Hereafter. It is particularly significant in the context of the Minor and Major Occultation, as it validates the endurance of the Shia through the martyrdom of the Ahl al-Bayt, with Imam Ali al-Husayn’s practice of linking their graves to the prophets serving as a tangible link to prophetic legacy.
